newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reed Elsevier has no plans to sell IPC magazines.
newsitem.headline: Reed Elsevier has no plans to sell IPC magazines.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed Elsevier said on Wednesday it did not plan to sell off its British IPC Magazines unit as part of a phased divestment of its consumer publishing operations.
"We are intending to hang on to IPC. There is absolutely no reason to divest it because it is such a leading business," co-chairman Herman Bruggink told an annual results presentation.
Reed Elsevier sold its newspapers in 1995 and plans to sell off its consumer books businesses in order to focus on more profitable scientific, business and professional publishing.

But Bruggink said there were no plans for the foreseeable future to sell IPC Magazines as part of this operation, noting that its operating margins of around 20 percent were close to the overall total for Reed Elsevier of 25.3 percent in 1996.
"It's a very profitable and succesful business. It comes close to the overall Reed Elsevier operating margin and is higher than some of the other activities we're involved in."
Unlike other consumer businesses sold by Reed Elsevier, IPC was a strong leader in its own market, he said.
Bruggink said IPC had "excellent" editorial content and "top class" editorial management, referring to "Loaded" and "Eat Soup" -- titles aimed at young men -- to illustrate his point.
